prisoner.name: Alfred Hassler
prisoner.description: Alfred Hassler was an editor and leader of the Fellowship of Reconciliation. His opposition to wartime conscription led to federal imprisonment in 1944–1945. He later published a prison diary and worked against the Vietnam War.

cases.charges: Refusal to comply with wartime conscription as a conscientious objector
cases.sentence: Imprisoned in 1944; paroled in March 1945. His diary documents detention in New York followed by Lewisburg. The full sentence and exact initial admission date are unresolved.

entries.custody_evidence: His diary contains prison entries spanning June through later months of 1944, followed by the documented March1945 parole.
entries.research_notes: July6 is the Lewisburg arrival, not initial custody. Incarceration_date stays blank to avoid calculating an exact duration from partial endpoints. Coordinates reuse the verified existing penitentiary record; no camp identity substituted.

prisoner.name: Lawrence Scott
prisoner.description: Lawrence Scott was a Quaker organizer and former American Friends Service Committee peace-education director. He led the Washington Peace Action Center and was jailed for a White House peace vigil. He later helped establish A Quaker Action Group.

cases.charges: White House peace-vigil prosecution; exact charge for the documented thirty-day term is unresolved
cases.sentence: His archival biography records a thirty-day jail term served during the Peace Action Center years, 1961–1963. This is not assigned the dates of the separate 1962 twenty-day sentence from which he was bailed pending appeal.

entries.custody_evidence: The institutional finding aid explicitly distinguishes a sentence actually served: thirty days in jail.
entries.research_notes: Several White House prosecutions appear in the sources. No unsupported date, extra case, or numerical aggregate is inferred. The undated thirty-day episode is retained separately from research leads about shorter sentences.

prisoner.name: Florence Y. Carpenter
prisoner.description: Florence Y. Carpenter was an Ohio Friend and Peace Action Center worker. She joined the 1962 White House vigil against nuclear tests and served twenty days in jail.

cases.charges: Disorderly conduct: congregating and refusing a police order to move; DC Code1961 section22-1121(2)
cases.sentence: Served twenty days in 1962. The convictions were affirmed October26,1962. Exact admission and release dates remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: Young explicitly reports completion of the twenty-day term.
entries.research_notes: Actual duration is retained in sentence text: the existing model has no durable source-only day counter. No invented endpoints or rounded month substitutes. AFSC or FOR membership is not inferred from association.

prisoner.name: Pearl C. Ewald
prisoner.description: Pearl C. Ewald was a Quaker peace activist and Peace Action Center worker. She was imprisoned after the 1962 White House nuclear-test vigil and later advocated war-tax resistance.
